text:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME reporting a really odd console heatmap — large swaths of tiles show 0 usage for the last 6 hours, but API usage logs show requests succeeded. link: https://console.redwood.internal/tenants/acme/heatmap :eyes:
ben_engineer: Can you paste the tenant id + a screenshot of the heatmap? Is this just the heatmap viz or missing rows in the usage table as well?
maria_support: tenant_id: tenant_acme_42. Screenshot attached in thread. Customer says hourly totals are present but per-hour heatmap == all zeros for 00:00-06:00 UTC. They noticed the dashboard updated earlier today then regressed after a retry/backfill.
infra-bot: [ALERT] etl-rollup-consumer lag increased for topic rollups-hourly (consumer=rollup-service-02) offset_lag=124567, last_commit=1794012000
carla_dataeng: I see errors in the rollup consumer around 1794012100 — auth token refresh failed against SSO. Error: `403 Forbidden: service account token invalidated (rotation)` then consumer retried and paused. That would cause recent windows to be skipped until backfill completed.
dave_oncall: Did any backfill job run? What was the status of the backfill?
maria_support: Support ran the quick backfill (job id bf-2026-04-01-17) that reported SUCCESS but customer still sees zeros.
ben_engineer: SUCCESS sometimes means rows were queued but not indexed into the viz materialized table. Can you share the backfill logs? Also give me a sample query we run to populate the heatmap.
maria_support: backfill logs (excerpt): ```2026-04-01T17:05:12Z INFO starting backfill job bf-2026-04-01-17
2026-04-01T17:12:03Z WARN partial-write: 24/360 partitions failed to enqueue
2026-04-01T17:13:00Z INFO job complete, processed 98% of expected windows
```
carla_dataeng: That WARN is the smoking gun — certain partitions failed to enqueue because the rollup producer saw `kafka: authorization failed` intermittently while the consumer was rotating keys. The producer retried but those partitions missed the atomic upsert into the viz table. We'll need to re-run a targeted rehydrate for tenant_acme_42 windows 00:00-06:00 UTC.
ben_engineer: Rehydrate plan: 1) Pause live rollup producer for tenant_acme_42 to avoid duplicate writes. 2) Run targeted rehydrate for those hourly windows. 3) Validate counts in `hourly_usage_rollup` and then trigger viz rebuild.
dave_oncall: I'll take step 1. pausing now... `kubectl scale deployment rollup-producer --replicas=0 -n prod-rollups`
infra-bot: [ACTION] rollout pause command accepted by k8s controller at 1794012365
maria_support: Customer is nervous about repeated zeros in heatmap. Can we give an ETA?
carla_dataeng: ETA: rehydrate job ~15-25m, then validation 5m, viz rebuild 10m. Total ~40-45m if no further issues. I'll start the targeted rehydrate and post logs.
ben_engineer: After rehydrate we should run this check: ```SELECT hour, count(*) FROM hourly_usage_rollup WHERE tenant_id='tenant_acme_42' AND hour >= '2026-04-01T00:00:00Z' AND hour < '2026-04-01T07:00:00Z' GROUP BY hour;``` compare to API-side raw request counts.
maria_support: noted. looping in account exec and sent initial update to customer: "We've identified a producer auth rotation gap causing missed partitions; running targeted rehydrate, ETA ~45m. Will update when heatmap fixed." :white_check_mark:
carla_dataeng: starting rehydrate now. job id rehydrate-1794012375, tailing logs...
carla_dataeng: log snippet: ```2026-04-01T17:39:10Z INFO rehydrate window 00:00 -> 01:00 enqueued
2026-04-01T17:41:02Z INFO rehydrate window 00:00 -> 01:00 complete (rows=1203)
2026-04-01T17:48:05Z INFO rehydrate completed for windows 00:00-06:00, total_rows=7345
```
dave_oncall: scaling rollup-producer back to 2 replicas
ben_engineer: run the validation query and then invalidate viz cache: `POST /internal/visuals/invalidate?tenant=tenant_acme_42&visual=heatmap`
carla_dataeng: validation results: counts match expected from raw logs. Triggering viz invalidation.
maria_support: customer confirms heatmap now shows values for missing tiles. Customer happy. Closing loop and will follow up with a postmortem on auth rotation safeguards. :tada:
